requirement: Symmetric encryption utility enforcing authenticated AES-GCM mode with random 12-byte nonces, associated data authentication, and explicit rejection of insecure ECB mode.
skeleton: AuthenticatedCipher class with encrypt and decrypt methods using cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead.AESGCM.

rationale.teaches: AES-GCM with a random 12-byte nonce per message, associated data bound into the tag, 16 or 32 byte keys only, nonce length checked on decrypt, and InvalidTag turned into a ValueError.
rationale.why: ECB and a fixed nonce both encrypt and decrypt round-trip perfectly; the flaw only shows when two ciphertexts are compared. The fixture encrypts the same plaintext twice and expects different bytes and a tag failure when the associated data changes.

candidates.why_wrong: AES-ECB replaces GCM, so identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks and there is no integrity tag.
The nonce is all zeros, so two messages with the same key reuse the nonce and the keystream is recoverable.
Decrypt passes None as associated data, so a message whose associated data was tampered still decrypts.
8-byte keys are accepted and zero-padded to 16, so a 64-bit key masquerades as AES-128.
Nonce length is not checked on decrypt, so a wrong-length nonce raises ValueError from the library instead of a clear validation error.
